name: bedtime-stories-story
description: >-
  Use when it's time for tonight's bedtime story (nightly routine or a parent's
  ask): write a short, personalized, age-appropriate story starring the child.
---
# Bedtime story

## Inputs
- Child profile from memory: first name, age, favorite things, things to avoid, recurring friends/pets/toys, the character sheet.
- Tonight's theme from the parent (a fear, a lesson, an event of the day). If none was given, pick one from memory that hasn't been used recently, or a gentle default (sharing, trying something new, saying goodnight to the day).
- Past story titles (from memory or the Storybook Page) so you don't repeat plots.

## Structure
1. Cozy opening: a familiar, safe place, the child by name, one favorite thing.
2. A small, low-stakes problem tied to the theme. Never danger, injury, getting lost for long, monsters that win, death, or parents in trouble.
3. The child's own brave, kind or clever choice solves it. A helper (favorite animal or toy) can assist, but the child acts.
4. Wind-down: pace slows, sentences shorten, things get quiet and sleepy (stars, blankets, yawns, soft breathing).
5. Final sleepy line addressed to the child, e.g. "Goodnight, [name]. Sleep tight."

## Length (3-5 minutes read aloud)
- Age 2-3: about 250-350 words, simple words, gentle repetition.
- Age 4-5: about 400 words.
- Age 6-9: about 600-700 words, a little more plot and dialogue.

## Rules
- Respect the avoid list absolutely. If a theme is a fear (dark, new school, doctor), make the feared thing turn out friendly and manageable, never confirm it.
- No brand characters or copyrighted characters by name; invent originals inspired by what the child likes.
- Give the story a short title.
- Mark 3-4 scene beats (opening, problem, brave choice, sleepy ending) for illustration.

## After writing
Send the title and story text in chat, then run bedtime-stories-illustrate, then bedtime-stories-read-aloud, then add it to the Storybook Page. Save a one-line journal memory: date, title, theme.

skills.description: Use right after a bedtime story is written: generate 3-4 soft storybook illustrations with the same child character every time.

name: bedtime-stories-illustrate
description: >-
  Use right after a bedtime story is written: generate 3-4 soft storybook
  illustrations with the same child character every time.
---
# Illustrate the story

## Character sheet (keep in memory)
On the first story, write a short character sheet and save it to profile memory, then reuse it word for word every night:
- Child as an illustrated character: age look, hair color/style, skin tone, a signature outfit item (e.g. yellow raincoat). Ask the parent for these details; never guess from a name.
- Recurring companions (favorite animal or toy) with fixed colors.
- Style line: "soft watercolor children's picture-book illustration, warm pastel palette, gentle lighting, rounded shapes, cozy, no text".

## Steps
1. Take the 3-4 scene beats from the story.
2. For each, call GenerateImage with: style line + character sheet + the scene (place, action, mood). Keep the last scene dim and calm (night, lamp light, stars).
3. Look at each image. Regenerate once if the character drifts badly, anything looks scary, or there is garbled text.
4. Send the images in one message under the story, in story order.

## Rules
- Illustrated characters only. Never make photorealistic images of the child, and never use real photos unless the parent uploads one and asks for it as a likeness reference.
- Nothing frightening: no sharp teeth, dark shadows looming, or distressed faces.
- Keep image files for the Storybook Page.

skills.name: bedtime-stories-read-aloud
skills.description: Use after the story and pictures are sent: deliver the story as a calm, slow voice memo the parent can play at bedtime, then save it to the Storybook Page.
skills.content:
---
name: bedtime-stories-read-aloud
description: >-
  Use after the story and pictures are sent: deliver the story as a calm, slow
  voice memo the parent can play at bedtime, then save it to the Storybook Page.
---
# Read aloud

1. Load the Cursor-managed `voice` skill and follow it.
2. Content: the title, then the story text as written, in spoken sentences. Drop scene markers and formatting. Keep the child's name and the sleepy final line.
3. Aim for a gentle, unhurried pace: short sentences, natural pauses at paragraph breaks, softer and slower toward the end.
4. Send it as the voice memo message.
5. Add tonight's story to the Storybook Page (load the `canvas` skill): one entry per night with date, title, the theme, the pictures and the text, newest first. Edit the existing Storybook Page instead of making a new one; create it only on the first story.
6. Stories stay private: only in this chat and the Storybook Page. Never post or send them anywhere else unless the parent asks.

# Getting started

I make bedtime easier: a short story starring your child, with pictures and a voice note, saved to a keepsake storybook.

Open with: "Tell me your child's name, age and three favorite things. Tonight they'll get a story starring them, with pictures and a voice note you can play."

Then ask, one at a time, only what's still missing:
1. Child's first name and age.
2. Three favorite things (animals, places, toys, colors).
3. Anything to avoid (fears, topics, words).
4. What the child looks like for the illustrated character (hair, skin tone, a favorite outfit), or say I'll invent a look.
5. Anything on their mind today to weave in (a fear, a lesson, an event). Optional.

Save answers to profile memory (one fact each; several children get separate facts). Never ask for photos; use one only if the parent uploads it.

As soon as you have name, age and favorites, write the first story right away: run bedtime-stories-story, bedtime-stories-illustrate, bedtime-stories-read-aloud, and create the Storybook Page.

Then offer the nightly routine in one sentence: "Want me to check in every evening at 7pm for tonight's theme and have the story ready?" On yes, load the `routines` skill and create a daily routine at the time they pick (default 19:00 their time) whose prompt is: ask the parent for tonight's theme (or pick one from memory if they don't answer), then run bedtime-stories-story, illustrate, read-aloud, and add it to the Storybook Page.
